case_title.quote: Sham @ Kishor Bhaskarrao Matkari v. State of Maharashtra
case_title.reason: Case title matches the judgment heading.

number_of_accused.reason: Single accused is referred to throughout.

accused_gender.quote: he had no pre-plan to do away with the family of his brother
accused_gender.reason: Accused is referred to as male throughout.

accused_age.quote: the accused was 28 years old and was jobless
accused_age.reason: Court states age 28; para 12 records counsel's claim of 38, but the Court's own finding is 28.

accused_religion.reason: Religion is not mentioned in the judgment.

accused_caste.reason: Caste is not mentioned in the judgment.

accused_occupation.quote: the accused was 28 years old and was jobless
accused_occupation.reason: Judgment describes accused as jobless at time of incident.

previous_criminal_record.quote: the antecedents of the accused-appellant are unblemished
previous_criminal_record.reason: Court finds unblemished antecedents and no prior criminal activity.

victim_gender.quote: Manohar, his wife Meena, daughter Monika and son Vishwesh
victim_gender.reason: Victims include both male and female members, so 'Mixed' is supported.

victim_age.reason: Victims' ages are not stated; children are only described as small or young.

accused_victim_relationship.quote: The appellant-accused was the real brother of Manohar Matkari-the deceased
accused_victim_relationship.reason: Accused was brother of the deceased; other victims were his family members.

offence_category.quote: conviction under Section 302 IPC for murder
offence_category.reason: Offence is murder under s.302 with attempt under s.307.

statutory_provisions.quote: for the offences punishable under Sections 302, 307 and 201 of the Indian Penal Code
statutory_provisions.reason: Sections 302, 307 and 201 are correctly listed, with s.201 acquittal noted.

weapon.quote: a stone of big size and a gas cylinder with tube were lying near her body
weapon.reason: Stone and gas cylinder are recorded; Court states no dangerous weapon was used.

evidence_type.quote: There is no reason to disbelieve the version of Monika (PW-7) ... neighbours and landlord ... confessional statement
evidence_type.reason: Eyewitness, medical, recovery and confessional evidence are all relied on.

confession.quote: the statement recorded by the Executive Magistrate had been treated as statement under Section 164
confession.reason: Hospital statement to Executive Magistrate treated as s.164 statement and relied upon.

aggravating_circumstances.quote: (iii) The assault on victims by the respondent was aimed at midnight when the victims were fast asleep
aggravating_circumstances.reason: Listed aggravating circumstances are the High Court's findings recited by the Supreme Court.

mitigating_circumstances.quote: the quarrel started due to the land dispute and ... he was sleeping with the other victims in the same house
mitigating_circumstances.reason: Mitigating factors match those the Court relied on in para 14.

trial_court_outcome.quote: sentenced him to imprisonment for life and to pay a fine of Rs.25,000/-
trial_court_outcome.reason: Life term, fines, 7 years RI under s.307 and s.201 acquittal are all supported.

high_court_outcome.quote: the High Court dismissed the appeal filed by the appellant-accused and allowed the appeal filed by the State and enhanced the sentence
high_court_outcome.reason: Accused's appeal dismissed, State's appeal allowed, life sentence enhanced to death.

final_outcome.correct_value: Conviction maintained; death sentence set aside and life imprisonment restored
final_outcome.quote: while maintaining the conviction of the appellant-accused for the offence under Section 302 IPC, award of extreme penalty of death by the High Court is set aside
final_outcome.reason: Conviction was upheld, not modified; only the sentence was altered.

offence_finally_established.quote: we are in entire agreement with the said conclusion
offence_finally_established.reason: Court upholds conviction under ss.302 and 307 as stated in para 10.

imprisonment_type.quote: we restore the sentence of life imprisonment as directed by the trial Court

imprisonment_years.reason: Life imprisonment has no fixed term, so null is consistent with the judgment.

fine_rs.quote: sentenced him to imprisonment for life and to pay a fine of Rs.25,000/-
fine_rs.reason: Judgment records fines of Rs.25,000 and Rs.1,000, so null is wrong.

neutral_facts.quote: He sent the accused to the hospital for treatment in a police jeep
neutral_facts.reason: Facts match the judgment and do not reveal the Supreme Court's sentencing outcome.

offence_severity.reason: No formal severity classification is given; 'cold-blooded murders' is a High Court characterization only.

attempt_completion.reason: Three murders completed; s.307 attempt on the two surviving children.

physical_harm.quote: victim Manohar and his wife Meenabai died on the spot having suffered head injuries
physical_harm.reason: Deaths, head injuries, burns and two injured children are supported.

number_of_offences.quote: for the offences punishable under Sections 302, 307 and 201
number_of_offences.reason: Three sections were registered and s.302 and s.307 finally upheld.

financial_property_loss.reason: No property loss value is stated; only the accused's story mentions household articles taken.

premeditation_planning.quote: it must be said that the assault was pre-meditated
premeditation_planning.reason: High Court found premeditation; Supreme Court held no pre-plan and found High Court reasons inadequate.

motive.quote: The quarrel started due to the land dispute
motive.reason: Land/property dispute is the accepted motive.

key_evidence_accepted.quote: Considering the opinion of the doctors, cause of death and recovery of a stone inside the house
key_evidence_accepted.reason: Listed evidence matches what the Court accepted.

witness_credibility.quote: There is no reason to disbelieve the version of Monika (PW-7)
witness_credibility.reason: Court found PW-7, PW-1, PW-3 and doctors credible.

post_offence_conduct.quote: This plea of the respondent (original accused) was found to be false
post_offence_conduct.reason: Three-thieves story recorded as found false; hospital confession noted.

custody_duration.quote: He is in jail since 30.06.2001 and in the death cell since the date of the judgment of the High Court
custody_duration.reason: Custody dates and durations match the judgment.

bail_history.reason: Bail history is not mentioned in the judgment.

trial_duration.reason: Offence, trial, High Court and Supreme Court dates are all supported.

legal_representation.quote: Tara Chand Sharma, Mahabir Singh Mangla, Uma Datta, Kishan Datta and Neelam Sharma for the Appellant
legal_representation.reason: Counsel names for both sides match the judgment.

investigation_status.quote: charge-sheet was laid in the Court of Judicial Magistrate
investigation_status.reason: FIR, investigation, charge-sheet and completed trial are all supported.

procedural_irregularity.reason: The judgment notes no procedural irregularity, though the statement was treated as s.164 despite not being a dying declaration.

appeal_history.quote: the High Court dismissed the appeal preferred by the appellant-accused and allowed the appeal preferred by the State
appeal_history.reason: Trial, High Court and Supreme Court outcomes are accurately recorded.

prosecution_argument.quote: in view of death of three persons and causing injuries to two, all in one family, the High Court was justified
prosecution_argument.reason: State's argument on three deaths and two injuries is accurately recorded.

defence_argument.quote: in view of several mitigating circumstances ... the extreme penalty of death is not warranted
defence_argument.reason: Defence argument on mitigating circumstances and rarest of rare is accurately recorded.

legal_principle_applied.quote: it is not a rarest of rare case where extreme penalty of death is called for
legal_principle_applied.reason: Rarest of rare test, balancing and adequate reasons requirement are all applied.

precedent_relied_upon.quote: Ajitsingh Hamamsingh Gujral vs. State of Maharashtra, JT 2011 (10) SC 465 - distinguished
precedent_relied_upon.reason: Precedents and treatment (distinguished vs referred) match the judgment.

sentencing_rationale.quote: the reasonings assigned by the High Court for awarding extreme penalty of death sentence are not acceptable
sentencing_rationale.reason: Rationale matches the Court's reasoning in para 14.

judicial_mitigating_factors.quote: there is no reason to disbelieve that the appellant cannot be reformed or rehabilitated
judicial_mitigating_factors.reason: Mitigating factors match para 14; the reformability point is a fair paraphrase.

judicial_aggravating_factors.quote: Though the appellant caused death of three persons
judicial_aggravating_factors.reason: Court acknowledges three deaths and rejects the High Court's death-sentence reasoning.

other_sentence_order.reason: No other sentence order is recorded beyond the life sentence restoration.
